title: A Time Capsule for America's 250th Birthday Will Stay Buried Until 2276!
summary: What would you put in a box for kids 250 years from now? That's the big question behind America's 250th birthday time capsule. On July 4, 2026, a special steel capsule will be buried near Independence Hall in Philadelphia — the very spot where the Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776. It won't be opened until July 4, 2276, when the country turns 500! Every state and territory sent something to go inside. The items are a wild mix. Arkansas sent a real diamond. Maine added a bone from an endangered whale. Wisconsin contributed a feather from "Old Abe," a famous bald eagle that helped Union soldiers during the Civil War. California went high-tech: a computer chip and an AI-generated guess about what the state will look like in 2276. Utah went all out with over 100 items, including coins, pins, and granite disks. Keeping everything safe for 250 years is a huge challenge. A team of experts built the capsule to be super tough. One engineer said Philadelphia would have to be under six feet of water before the capsule could even get wet! To help future people find it, a giant snake-shaped sculpture — inspired by Benjamin Franklin's "Join, or Die" cartoon — will mark the spot. Inside, the very first thing they'll see is a letter that says, "Greetings from the living, breathing hearts and hands of 2026... We built this for you."
why_it_matters: Thinking about what you would put in a box for kids 250 years from now might make you wonder what your toys, games, or drawings say about your life today.

background_read: Independence Hall in Philadelphia is the very building where the Declaration of Independence was signed on July 4, 1776—the paper that said America would be its own country.
Benjamin Franklin was one of the Founding Fathers and also drew the famous 'Join, or Die' cartoon, a picture of a snake cut into pieces to encourage the colonies to work together.
Time capsules have been used for over a hundred years to save a little bit of today and send a message to the people of the future.
Article_Structure: WHO: All 50 U.S. states and territories, plus a team of experts who built the capsule.
WHAT: A steel time capsule will be buried on July 4, 2026, filled with a wild mix of items from across the country.
WHERE: Near Independence Hall in Philadelphia, where the Declaration of Independence was signed.
WHY: To celebrate America's 250th birthday and give people in the year 2276 a real look at life in 2026.

perspectives.description: Many people love the idea of sending a piece of today into the future as a gift, making a direct link across hundreds of years.
Some might say that picking a diamond or a bone does not really show everyday life, and the capsule might miss the most important parts of our culture.
The team building the capsule must solve huge problems like water, rust, and heat so that the treasures inside survive the long wait and are still exciting for the future finders.
